slots.metaTitle: What Makes a Good Photo for an Anime Portrait?
slots.title: Good Photo for an Anime Portrait: Before-and-After Guide
slots.description: Learn what makes a good photo for an anime portrait, including lighting, clarity, expression, framing and selfie tips for a hand-drawn custom transformation.
slots.intro:
The best anime transformations begin with a photo that gives an artist clear information to work from. A good photo for an anime portrait shows your face clearly, uses even lighting and captures the expression or pose you want to preserve. It does not need to be a professional studio photograph.

At Anime Cabinet, human artists draw each custom anime portrait from your uploaded reference photo. We do not apply an AI filter or automatically replace your features. Instead, your likeness becomes an original character within the visual language of your chosen style. You can choose from 24 anime and cartoon styles, including [Demon Slayer](/portraits/demon-slayer), [Ghibli Style](/portraits/ghibli-style), [Naruto](/portraits/naruto) and [One Piece](/portraits/one-piece). Preview artwork arrives within 72 hours, and unlimited free revisions are included so you can request adjustments before approving the final piece.

[{"heading":"1. Choose a clear, high-resolution photo","content":"The most important quality in a custom anime portrait from photo is visibility. Your artist needs to see the shape of your face, eyes, eyebrows, hairstyle and distinctive features. Choose the sharpest original image you have rather than a screenshot saved from social media, where compression may blur small details. A recent phone photo is usually suitable if it is in focus and large enough to show facial features clearly.

Avoid images with heavy filters, stickers, motion blur or extreme beauty effects. These can hide the details that help an artist create a recognisable original character. If you are ordering a custom anime portrait canvas, a larger source file is especially helpful because the artwork may be viewed at a bigger size.","heading":"2. Use soft, even lighting","content":"What lighting works best for a custom anime or cartoon portrait? Soft, balanced light from a window or an open outdoor area usually works well. Face the light rather than standing with a bright window directly behind you. This keeps your eyes, nose, jawline and skin tone visible without creating deep shadows.

Harsh overhead lighting, coloured nightclub light and strong sunlight can make facial details difficult to interpret. You do not need elaborate equipment: a shaded outdoor spot or a bright room with indirect daylight is often enough. If you take a new photo, avoid using the phone flash close to your face unless the room is genuinely too dark.","heading":"3. Keep your face unobstructed","content":"A good photo for anime portrait work normally shows your full face without sunglasses, a hand covering your cheek or hair hiding both eyes. Glasses are fine if you wear them regularly, and hats can be included when they are part of the look you want illustrated. If you would like the final character without glasses or with a different hairstyle, mention that in your order notes.

For facial details to translate well, make sure the eyebrows, eyes, nose, mouth and jawline are not obscured. You can send more than one reference photo if one image shows your hairstyle best and another shows your expression or face shape more clearly.","heading":"4. Pick an expression and pose with intention","content":"Your expression helps set the mood of the finished portrait. A relaxed smile, confident look, playful pose or serious expression can all work. Choose the photo that feels most like the result you want, rather than assuming a passport-style image is required.

For a head-and-shoulders commission, a three-quarter angle can add personality while still showing enough of your face. A straight-on image is useful when accurate facial symmetry matters. If you want a dynamic full-body composition, include a second reference that clearly shows your posture, clothing or general proportions.","heading":"5. Selfies can be good reference photos","content":"Can I use a selfie as a good photo for an anime portrait? Yes. A selfie can work very well when it is sharp, well lit and taken without an extreme wide-angle distortion. Hold the phone at approximately eye level and avoid placing it too close to your face. A timer photo taken from a little farther away may show your proportions more naturally.

Some front-facing phone cameras subtly stretch the centre of the image or enlarge features near the lens. This is not always a problem, but if your nose or forehead looks unusually prominent, send another photo for comparison. Our artists can use multiple references to understand your features while following your preferred expression and pose.","heading":"6. Close-up or full-body: which is better?","content":"The right framing depends on the product. A close-up or upper-body photo is usually best for a face-focused custom anime portrait. It gives the artist more information about your expression and facial details. A full-body photo is useful when you want a complete character pose, specific clothing, shoes or a themed action scene.

You can provide both. For example, use a clear close-up as the main likeness reference and add a full-body image for outfit and pose guidance. If your chosen composition needs a different crop, include a short note at checkout so the artist knows which details matter most.","heading":"7. What if the photo is old or low quality?","content":"An old photograph can still be useful for a custom anime portrait commission online, especially when it captures a meaningful person or memory. However, the artist may have less information when the image is pixelated, faded, dark or very small. Send the original file if possible, along with any newer photo that shows the person’s current features.

Do not worry if your reference is not perfect. During the review process, we can tell you whether another image would help. Preview artwork is provided within 72 hours, and unlimited free revisions let you request reasonable changes to details such as hair, clothing, expression or colour.","heading":"8. Photo checklist before you upload","content":"Before placing an order, check that your reference photo is in focus, well lit and free from distracting filters. Make sure the face or pose you want is visible, and decide whether the final artwork should show a close-up, half-body or full-body composition. Add notes about important details such as freckles, glasses, tattoos, hairstyle, clothing or a preferred background.

These simple steps help whether you are ordering a custom anime portrait Australia customers can gift locally or arranging a commission online from elsewhere. You may see inexpensive custom anime portrait free tools or marketplace listings on Etsy, but an automated filter is different from a hand-drawn artwork reviewed by a human artist. Anime Cabinet creates an original fan-art-inspired character rather than copying or impersonating a copyrighted character.

If you like a particular series’ energy, you can request a style inspired by it—for example, bold shonen action, supernatural drama or a soft storybook feeling—while your portrait remains uniquely yours. Explore [Jujutsu Kaisen](/portraits/jujutsu-kaisen), [Dragon Ball Z](/portraits/dragon-ball-z) or [Attack on Titan](/portraits/attack-on-titan) for examples of themed directions.","heading":"Frequently asked questions","content":"What makes a good photo for an anime portrait commission? A sharp, well-lit image with a visible face, natural expression and minimal obstruction is the strongest starting point.

What kind of photo is best for a custom anime portrait? Use a recent, high-resolution photo that shows the features, pose or outfit you want represented. Send multiple angles when helpful.

How clear does my photo need to be? It should be clear enough to identify facial features without zooming into heavy pixelation. Professional quality is not necessary.

What facial details should be visible? Ideally, the eyes, eyebrows, nose, mouth, jawline and hairstyle should be visible. Distinctive details such as freckles or glasses can be included in your notes.

Should I send a close-up or full-body photo? Send a close-up for a face-focused piece and a full-body reference for clothing or pose. Providing both is often best."}]
